Meta.title: Diplodoctor — understand your medical reports
Meta.description: Diplodoctor reads a lab report with you: every value, which ones are outside their range, and what to ask. Any AI model, and, when you want a person, a health assistant or a licensed professional of your choice.

Footer.tagline: The health layer of the fleet: an agent that reads the report, and the people you choose to help.
Footer.disclaimer: Beta: running, not released. Diplodoctor gives health information, not a diagnosis, and is not a medical device or a substitute for a doctor. In an emergency, call your emergency number.
Footer.openSource: Open source under the MIT licence. Built in Zürich.

Settings.metaDescription: Use your own AI model for Diplodoctor readings.
Settings.title: Settings
Settings.p1: Without a key, Diplodoctor reads reports with free shared models. They have a small daily budget that every visitor draws on, and they are not the strongest available.
Settings.p2: A medical report deserves the best reading you can give it. Connect an API key from a provider below and your readings run on the strongest model that key can use, on your own budget. The key is kept in this browser only: it is sent with each reading to reach your provider and is never stored by Diplodoctor.
Settings.p3: Use an API key, ideally one with a spending cap. Diplodoctor never asks for a subscription login such as Claude Pro or ChatGPT Plus.

reports.name: Read a medical report

Platform.metaDescription: How Diplodoctor is built, what each part does and where it stops.
Platform.title: How Diplodoctor is built, and why
Platform.lede: A short, honest account of the parts, what each one does and where it stops. Every sentence describes code in this repository as it is today; what is planned is labelled and points to the roadmap.

why.title: Why it is built this way
why.p1: A lab report is a table of numbers with a range printed beside each. The hard part for a person is not the table; it is knowing what to ask, and trusting the answer.
why.p2: A language model is good at reading the table and at saying in plain words what a measurement is for. It is the wrong tool for deciding whether 5.8 is above 5.6. So the model reads, and code compares.
why.p3: And only a licensed professional may give medical advice where you are treated. A person who is not licensed can still help, and the product says what each one is. Diplodoctor is built to prepare that conversation, not to replace it.

architecture.title: Five parts, each with one job

intake.title: Intake
intake.body: A text box and up to four page photos, made smaller in your browser. Nothing is sent until you press the button.

redaction.title: Redaction
redaction.body: lib/redact.ts finds names, birth dates, addresses, insurance, order and phone numbers and replaces each with a placeholder, in the browser. You see every one and can switch it off.

reading.title: Reading
reading.body: One route calls ai-kit's complete() over the shared free chain, or your own key. The model returns one JSON object: values, units, ranges, the line each came from, plain-language information and questions.

checks.title: Checks
checks.body: The report schema, not the model, decides each flag by comparing the value with the printed bounds, and never lets the urgency fall below what the flags imply. A value is never shown without the line it was read from.

file.title: The file
file.body: One zod schema is the report: what the model produces, what the browser stores and what Export writes. A file that can leave is a file that belongs to you.

turn.title: One reading, step by step
turn.lede: What happens between pressing the button and seeing the result.
turn.s1: Your browser finds the personal details in the text and replaces them with placeholders.
turn.s2: Only the anonymised text and your page photos go to the server.
turn.s3: The server asks a model, from the free chain or your own key, to read the report. Nothing about it is stored or logged.
turn.s4: The reply is checked against the schema, and every flag is recomputed from the numbers.
turn.s5: Your browser puts the real values back where the placeholders were.
turn.s6: The report is saved in this browser. The server has already forgotten it.

information.title: Information, not diagnosis
information.body: The model is told never to diagnose, advise on medicines or reassure. The product repeats it wherever a result is shown.

honest.title: Nothing is claimed that is not true
honest.body: Every capability has a status in one file, and the pages read it. Nobody is listed, rated or quoted who does not exist.

open.title: Open source
open.body: The code, the prompt and the tests are public under the MIT licence, so a claim here can be checked there.

shared.title: Shared ground
shared.body: Design, models, limits and records come from packages the whole fleet uses, not from copies.

stack.title: The stack
stack.lede: The same column of packages as the rest of the fleet.

Security.metaDescription: What protects a medical report on Diplodoctor, and what does not.
Security.title: What protects a report here
Security.lede: Health data is among the most sensitive data there is; Swiss law calls it «besonders schützenswert». Here is what is done about it, and where the limits are.

anon.title: Anonymised before it leaves
anon.body: The model needs the values, not who they belong to.
anon.d1: Names, birth dates, addresses, phone numbers, e-mail, IBAN, AHV and insurance numbers, and patient and order numbers are replaced with placeholders in your browser.
anon.d2: You see each replacement before sending, can switch any off and can add words of your own.
anon.d3: The table of what each placeholder stands for never leaves your device.
anon.d4: Detection is deliberately generous: hiding one word too many costs a little detail; one too few would send your data.
anon.d5: Photos are not read in the browser, so they are sent as they are unless you cover the details first.

browser.title: Kept on your device
browser.body: Your reports live in this browser's storage.
browser.d1: There is no account and no copy of your reports on our server.
browser.d2: Clearing this site's data deletes them; export a file first if you want to keep one.
browser.d3: Anyone with access to this browser profile can read them.

minimal.title: Nothing kept on the server
minimal.body: The server passes a request through and forgets it.
minimal.d1: The anonymised text goes to a model provider for one request; the server stores nothing and logs only which model answered.
minimal.d2: Requests are rate limited per caller to protect the shared free tier.
minimal.d3: A model provider sees the anonymised text, so read its terms. With your own key it goes to your provider instead.

transport.title: A browser told to trust little
transport.body: The page is served with strict headers.
transport.d1: Scripts run only from this site and only with this response's nonce; requests go only to this site.
transport.d2: HTTPS only for two years; no framing; no referrer leaves the site.
transport.d3: No analytics and no third-party scripts.

model.title: Your key stays yours
model.body: If you connect your own model:
model.d1: The key is kept in this browser only and sent with each reading to reach your provider.
model.d2: It is never stored or logged by the server.

breach.title: If something goes wrong
breach.lede: What each failure would expose, said plainly.

provider.title: A model provider is breached
provider.body: It could expose the anonymised text of readings sent to it: values and dates without your name, address or numbers, unless a photo went uncovered.

operator.title: We are compromised
operator.body: There is no database of reports to steal. An attacker could change the site to send data elsewhere, which is why the code is public and the headers are checked after every deploy.

device.title: Your device is lost or shared
device.body: Your reports are readable by anyone who can open this browser. Use a device lock, and delete what you no longer need.

Ecosystem.metaDescription: Diplodoctor is the health layer of a fleet of products — OrangeCat, Loki and Solon — that one OrangeCat account opens.
Ecosystem.title: One person, a whole fleet
Ecosystem.lede: Diplodoctor is one product in a fleet built to give a single person what used to take an institution. Each product does one job, and one OrangeCat account opens them all.
Ecosystem.unavailable: The list of products could not be loaded just now. Try again in a minute.
Ecosystem.layerBody: OrangeCat moves value, Loki gets the work done and Solon governs. Diplodoctor is the health layer on top: the reports, records and appointments through which a person understands their own body and brings a doctor in.

account.title: One account
account.body: Sign-in with OrangeCat is planned for health matters. Reading a report needs no account today.

pay.title: Paid on OrangeCat
pay.body: Assistants and licensed professionals will offer their work as OrangeCat services and be paid there, in any currency.

build.title: Built with Loki
build.body: Loki builds and ships Diplodoctor and holds its identity.

law.title: Disputes go to Causius
law.body: When a report turns into a dispute with an insurer or an employer, the legal layer, Causius, takes it from there.

account.title: No account needed today
account.body: Reading a report needs none, and nothing about it is on our server. When health matters arrive, the same OrangeCat account that opens the rest of the fleet will open them.

People.metaDescription: Health assistants and licensed professionals: how people will help alongside Diplodoctor, and what each is allowed to say.
People.title: A person, when you want one
People.lead: Diplodoctor's AI explains a report. You may want a person too. The two kinds differ in who may say what, not in who is better. You decide whom to ask.
People.noneBody: Nobody has joined yet, so nobody is shown. There are no invented profiles or ratings here, and there will not be. For now, export the anonymised file and take it to someone you trust.

assistant.name: Health assistant
assistant.does1: Explains in plain words, in your language
assistant.does2: Shares experience and their view, for a price they set
assistant.doesNot: Their view is an opinion, not medical advice. They may or may not hold a health qualification and say so.
assistant.checks: Shown with how helpful people found them.

licensed.name: Licensed professional
licensed.identity: a verified licence, and a name or a pseudonym
licensed.does1: Advises on what a result means for you
licensed.checks: Licence checked against the public register, and provable without revealing who they are (planned).

People.wantBody: Anyone can offer help as a service on OrangeCat and be paid there, in any currency. The labels, licence check and helpfulness record are not built yet.

clinic.title: Your patients' reports, read before the appointment
clinic.lead: A clinic could use Diplodoctor the way a patient does, and later on its own terms:
clinic.c1: Patients arrive with results read and questions written.
clinic.c2: A patient hands over their file by choice.
clinic.c3: A model inside your own walls: patient data never leaves.

label.title: Everyone is labelled
label.body: An assistant is shown as an assistant, a licensed professional as one. The label says what they may do, not who is better.

pseudonym.title: Names are optional on every side
pseudonym.body: Everyone may use a pseudonym. A licence can be proven without revealing who holds it (planned).

share.title: You decide what leaves
share.body: A person gets the anonymised file unless you share more.

place.title: Advice counts where it is licensed
place.body: Medical advice only counts from someone licensed where you are treated.
